name: Cello
subtitle: Humming, rhythm & first notes
promotional_text: Start making music with short humming and rhythm lessons, recorded examples, live pitch feedback and simple melodies. No instrument needed for the first lessons.
description:
Start making music, one short lesson at a time. Cello helps beginners practise humming, rhythm and their first cello notes.

HEAR, HUM AND MATCH
Listen to recorded human humming, try the note yourself and follow live pitch feedback. Review your take with a pitch chart, beginner-friendly stars and a short note on what to change.

FIND THE BEAT
Tap along with a steady pulse, learn two taps per beat and practise mixed rhythms. Timing charts show how your taps compare with the pattern.

LEARN MELODIES, LEVEL BY LEVEL
Ten levels lead from one hummed note to the opening of the Prelude from Bach's Cello Suite No. 1, slowed down for learning: Hot Cross Buns, Ode to Joy, Twinkle, Twinkle, Lightly Row, Old MacDonald, Yankee Doodle, the G major scale, then the Prelude's chords and opening bars. Listen first, tap the rhythm and meet the notes, then hum each phrase and the whole melody. Listen & Echo adds fresh two-note and three-note humming patterns.

START YOUR CELLO JOURNEY
Meet the parts of the cello and hear its four open strings. Every lesson you hum or listen to can also be played on the cello, with recorded cello examples to match. Cello recording includes video for your own review or optional sharing with a teacher. You can start the humming and rhythm lessons before you own an instrument.

SEE YOUR PROGRESS
Follow a clear lesson path and today’s practice suggestions. Earn a pass with two stars and a gold mark with three three-star attempts among your last five. Lessons stay available so you can return whenever you like.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, advertising, subscription or analytics. Recordings and progress stay on your device. You choose whether to export or share a take.

Ratings are beginner practice feedback. Pitch estimates can miss notes or choose the wrong octave. A teacher can help with cello setup, posture and bowing.
review_notes:
1. Screen recording: attached below (Attachment). It was made on an iPhone 13 Pro Max running the latest iOS, with this build installed from TestFlight. It starts by launching the app and shows the typical flow: the lesson path, a humming lesson with its recording and result, a rhythm round, a melody level, the cello option, Recordings and About. The app has no account registration, login or account deletion, no content shared between users, and no paid content.

2. Purpose and audience: Cello is a free practice app for beginners of any age who want to start making music: hum in tune, keep a steady beat and play their first notes on the cello. It helps people practise alone, between lessons or before they own an instrument, with feedback instead of guesswork. The app plays recorded examples, listens through the microphone, shows the pitch live, and rates each attempt with beginner-friendly stars and a short note on what to change. Ten levels lead from one hummed note to the opening of the Prelude from Bach's Cello Suite No. 1, slowed down for learning.

3. Instructions: no login, account, purchase or sample files are needed, and every lesson is open. The Music tab shows the path: Today's practice, then Levels 1 to 10. Start with Level 1, First sounds > Steady hum: tap Start lesson, play the example, tap Record, allow microphone access and hum along. The result shows a pitch chart, stars and feedback. Pulse, Two taps and Mixed rhythm are tapping rounds with haptics. Levels 2 to 10 (Hot Cross Buns to Prelude opening) each have Listen, Tap it, Meet the notes, Hum it and Whole melody. The Voice/Cello switch at the top of each humming, listening and melody lesson moves it to the cello, and Meet your cello shows the parts and plays the four open strings. Cello takes need a cello to score well, and they also ask for camera access to save a video for the learner's own review. The Recordings tab plays, shares (user-initiated, through the system share sheet) or deletes takes. About has the credits, sound sources and privacy policy.

4. External services: none. The app makes no network requests and has no server, analytics, advertising, accounts, payments or AI services. Pitch detection, scoring and the feedback text run entirely on the device, and recordings and progress stay there. Links in About open public web pages (privacy policy, support, licences) in the browser.

5. Regions: the app works the same in every country or region, with no regional differences in features or content. The interface is in English.

6. Third-party material: the app is not in a regulated field. Its bundled sounds are licensed and credited in About and in licence files inside the app. The human hum is an adapted excerpt of "Deep Humming Noise" by retropttam (Freesound, CC BY 3.0), and the cello notes come from VSCO 2 Community Edition (CC0 1.0). All melodies are traditional or in the public domain (Hot Cross Buns, Ode to Joy, Twinkle Twinkle, Lightly Row, Old MacDonald, Yankee Doodle, the G major scale, and the opening of J. S. Bach's Cello Suite No. 1, BWV 1007), encoded independently. No score edition or other performer's recording is bundled. Source code: https://github.com/RonildoBraga/cello
